updates.share_rationale: Fable review correction: CMS Chat is available to CMS staff (~6,700 of HHS's ~44k AI-eligible employees, ~15%), not 87% of HHS. Original share conflated "100% of CMS" with HHS-wide coverage.

updates.tool_name: Agentforce (Salesforce AI agents — IRS Office of Chief Counsel, Taxpayer Advocate Service, Office of Appeals)
updates.share_rationale: No published headcount for the three specific IRS offices covered (Chief Counsel, Taxpayer Advocate Service, Office of Appeals); using the project's unknown-tier fallback of 0.05 against IRS's ~75,000 department-wide workforce as a conservative default. Likely understates share within the specific offices where it is actually deployed.

HeaRT's public figures are a case-volume metric (500,000 cases/year processed), not a user headcount; using SSA's unknown-tier fallback of 0.05 as a conservative default for hearing-office staff, a subset of SSA's ~57,000-60,000 workforce.
19,000 HQ-launch users / 65,000 eligible (260,000 DHS workforce x 0.25 eligible-tier prior) = 0.29; consistent with the calculation used for the existing DHS/DHSChat wave-2 update.

updates.tool_name: ChatGPT and Claude (commercial GenAI) — DHS enterprise access
updates.share_rationale: Coverage is explicitly 'none' as of the May 2025 DHS CIO memo revoking commercial GenAI access department-wide; share set to 0.
Directly stated in source: 'roughly 70% of GSA employees are consistent users of the tools' (GSA Deputy Administrator Michael Lynch, June 2026).

USAi.gov's coverage metric here is the count of OTHER federal agencies onboarded to GSA's hosting platform (25+, with 16 more coming), not a share of GSA's own workforce; share_of_eligible is not applicable to this cross-government hosting metric.

updates.tool_name: Claude for Enterprise and Claude for Government (Anthropic OneGov agreement)
updates.share_rationale: This is a government-wide procurement/pricing offer administered by GSA, not a GSA-workforce usage metric, so share_of_eligible is not applicable here.
